ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a voltage-divider biased common-emitter amplifier circuit. The upper side is the +VCC power supply, RB1 is connected from +VCC to the base node, and RB2 is connected from the base node to ground; the collector of transistor VT is connected to +VCC through RC, and the emitter is grounded through RE; there are capacitors C1, C2, and CE at the input, output, and emitter bypass positions, and there is load RL on the right side. Reasoning: According to DC quiescent analysis, all capacitors are treated as open circuits and ignored. According to the specified method, treat RB1 and RB2 as a stiff voltage divider, then the base voltage VB = 12 × 10kΩ / (20kΩ + 10kΩ) = 4 V. Given UBEQ ≈ 0.6 V, so the emitter voltage VE = VB - UBEQ = 4 - 0.6 = 3.4 V. RE = 2 kΩ, therefore IE = VE / RE = 3.4 V / 2 kΩ = 1.7 mA. Also IE = (β + 1)IB, β = 50, so IBQ = 1.7 mA / 51 ≈ 0.0333 mA = 33.3 μA, rounded to about 34 μA.

method.method_draft: Ignore all capacitors for DC. Treat RB1 and RB2 as a stiff divider setting the base voltage: VB=12×10k/(20k+10k)=4 V. Use the transistor junction drop to get VE=VB−0.6=3.4 V. Since RE=2 kΩ, IE=3.4/2k=1.7 mA. Convert to base current using IE=(β+1)IB with β=50: IB≈1.7 mA/51≈33.3 μA, rounded to 34 μA.
